title: Clement Hofbauer (15 March)
hookLine: a baker's apprentice turned priest who helped renew the Church in Vienna

lines: A HOPE THAT TAKES YEARS TO RISE.
cards: Bread can't be hurried. Flour, water, yeast, then the long wait, the dough under a cloth doing work nobody can see. A baker learns to get up in the dark, do what can be done, and leave the rest alone.
Clement Hofbauer learned that trade as a young man in Moravia, in central Europe. He wanted to be a priest, but his family was poor, so he kneaded dough instead.
It would be years before anything he hoped for began to rise.

teach.h: A LONG, CROOKED ROAD TO THE PRIESTHOOD.
teach.b: Clement's road was long and crooked. He worked in a monastery bakery, tried life as a hermit, walked to Rome as a pilgrim, and finally, with help from generous strangers, studied for the priesthood.

In Rome he joined the Redemptorists, a young order of preachers, and was sent north to Warsaw. There he and his companions threw themselves into a city church: preaching, confessions, a school, a home for orphans.
A story is told from those years.

teach.h: WARSAW: ORPHANS, AND A SPAT-ON FACE.
teach.b: He went into a tavern to beg for his orphans, and a man spat in his face. Clement wiped it off and said, more or less, that was for me, now what will you give for my orphans?
The man was so shaken, the story goes, that he gave. Then the political tide turned.

The Warsaw community was shut down and the priests sent away. Clement ended up in Vienna as chaplain to a convent of nuns, hearing confessions and talking with students, artists and writers who came to his rooms.
Little of it looked like success.
But those conversations helped renew Catholic life in the city, and he is remembered as a patron of Vienna.

The Letter of James, in the Douay-Rheims, describes this patience: "Behold, the husbandman waiteth for the precious fruit of the earth." A baker would say: the dough is rising, even if you can't see it.
Clement didn't live to see his order firmly planted in Austria. It came after him.

how: Catholics keep 15 March as the feast of Saint Clement Mary Hofbauer, especially in Vienna, where he is a patron of the city, and among the Redemptorists, who honor him as a founder of their work north of the Alps.

games.q: you're begging in a tavern for your orphans. a man spits in your face. what do you do?
o: wipe it off and ask what he'll give for the orphans.
games.why: the story told about Clement: that was for me, now what will you give for my orphans? the man, shaken, gave.

practice: Find one thing in your life that isn't rising as fast as you'd like, a project, a habit, a friendship that's still shy, your own healing, and picture it like dough under a cloth: you've done your part, and work is going on that you can't see.
If you pray, hand it to God for today; if you don't, breathe, and let it rise without you for a while.
